title: Corrections and resource bounds for the Trotter quantum transport algorithm
abstract: We audit arXiv:2508.15691v2 and the published Quantum Science and Technology article *Trotter-based quantum algorithm for solving transport equations with exponentially fewer time-steps* by Zylberman, Fredon, Loureiro and Debbasch. Ten registered correction groups persist in the directly inspected journal PDF. Exact counterexamples refute conservation of spatial derivative norms for variable transport fields and the signed-overlap identity assigned to a controlled-SWAP circuit. Further corrections concern transport and Liouville signs, Fourier inversion, moment normalization, constants and index ranges. We retain finite-time regularity factors and apply established commutator reasoning to obtain a coefficient-aware finite-grid operator bound proportional to inverse mesh spacing rather than its square for smooth periodic coefficients. This sharpens the chosen comparison baseline without proving a complete repaired vector-norm theorem or disproving the usefulness of smooth-state analysis. Independent calculations reproduce the reported eight-point discretization errors and a separate periodic splitting diagnostic. A version concordance, attributed source statements and numerical provenance tables make the findings directly checkable. The journal's added Gaussian-width, circuit-cost and boundary qualifications are acknowledged. No end-to-end quantum advantage, general impossibility result or inference about unavailable implementation code is claimed.

novelty_statement: Version-specific correction audit of arXiv:2508.15691v2 with exact counterexamples, a constructive finite-time regularity replacement, a coefficient-aware finite-grid operator baseline, independent positive diagnostics and explicit implementation limits. Established transport, SWAP and commutator identities are identified as established ingredients, not new discoveries. The directly obtained journal PDF is also audited for all ten registered groups, which persist with their qualifications. The journal's added localization-width, implementation/output-cost and boundary discussions are credited. This is not a complete audit of every journal addition, a new quantum algorithm, or proof of implementation failure.
